research-topics.title: Complex Event Recognition
research-topics.description: Complex Event Recognition (CER) is a class of data management technologies where users are interested in recognizing complex events over data streams, namely, groups of events on a stream that represent critical situations in real life. In this line of work, I study the foundations of CER systems, starting with the query language for specifying patterns of complex events, continuing with the computational model for internally representing these patterns, and concluding with optimizing and efficiently evaluating these models.

research-topics.title: Information Extraction
research-topics.description: Extracting and transforming semi-structured data (like JSON, CSV, or plain text files) is a repetitive task in data-intensive workloads. To speed up this task, rule-based information extraction uses patterns (regex) to extract and transform data. In this line of research, I study the foundations of rule-based information extraction, enhancing classical regex and automata models with novel extraction mechanisms to enable a useful, efficient process for extracting and transforming data from text documents.

research-topics.title: Automata Theory
research-topics.description: Automata theory studies state-based computational models for computing patterns or functions over sequences. In my group, we apply automata theory to data management tasks on data structured as sequences (like text documents, streams, or paths in graph data). I also study the foundations of automata theory, exploring new models and properties, and proposing new algorithms for automata-related problems.

research-topics.title: Query Evaluation and Logic
research-topics.description: Data management systems store data in some format, and users interact with the system through some programming language to query it. Relational databases are probably the most popular systems for storing data structured as tables, and querying it using SQL. In this line of research, I study how to efficiently process these queries, such as SQL, relational algebra, or other query languages.

research-topics.title: Metrics for Structure Data
research-topics.description: In this line of work, I study interesting measures over relational or graph data, and how to compute them efficiently. For instance, I study scores to measure the centrality of nodes in a graph, or scores to measure the diversity of a set of results.

description: People and digital systems generates today data at high speed like sensors networks, stock markets, smart cities, or social networks, among others. These data sources are usually referred to as data streams: continuous sequences of data generated at high speed and without end. Complex Event Recognition (CER) is a class of technologies that model data streams as sequences of events, where users are interested in recognizing complex events, namely, groups of events on a stream that represent critical situations in real life. Examples of complex events could include a fire detected by a sensor network in a nature reserve, an accident recognized by cameras in a smart city, or a critical social event in a social network. To detect these complex event, a complex event recognition engine is a data management software that must efficiently process such data and alert on the presence of complex events in real time.

In this line of work, my group study the foundations of complex event recognition systems starting from the query language to specify patterns of complex events, continue with the computational model to internally represent such patterns, and the optimization and efficient evaluation of such models.
